source.title: Table2Image: Lightweight Tabular Learning with Generated Proxy Representations and Reliability Diagnostics
source.authors: Seungeun Lee; Kihwan Lee; Subin Bae; Sang-Jun Lee; Seul Lee; Julia Stoyanovich; Il-Youp Kwak; Seungsang Oh

record.file_problem: The supplied full text is readable; no relevant cut-off or garbling noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests training-label corruption in tabular models, but measures clean-test performance and instability rather than fitting a completely random labeling to zero training error. Its noisy-label intervention conceptually bears on V4.
record.gate_note: The paper corrupts training labels at expected rates 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 and reports test performance and prediction instability. It does not test fully random labels, training error across label-noise levels, unstructured inputs, regularization's necessity or sufficiency, or learning order. Its statement about training performance under noise is summarized across scenarios rather than broken out by noise severity.
record.test_reason: The study tests part of V4 in tabular classification: clean-test degradation under increasing random label corruption and aggregate training fit. Completely random labeling is not required to test this restricted part of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: Table2Image maintains favorable predictive performance under the tested corruptions, while relative degradation and realization-level stability vary by scenario. The authors characterize training fit as strong relative to comparators; they do not claim perfect noisy-label fitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses tabular data, internally constructed proxy targets, and partial expected label corruption, rather than random labels on image datasets or the original image-network protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies training label-noise ratio over 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20; results are aggregated across these levels for APS and WSP.

fits_no_version.finding: XGBoost and SVM preserve considerable clean-test performance under partial label corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-neural tabular classifiers retain predictive performance under partial random label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: T2I has favorable noisy-label test performance but comparatively high label corruption instability, with LCI 0.291.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aggregate robustness to label corruption can coexist with prediction variability across independent corruption realizations.

record.problems: The label-noise results aggregate performance across severities and do not report training fit separately at each level. Only partial corruption ratios up to 0.20 are tested; uncertainty estimates for these robustness aggregates are not stated.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, near-zero training error on them, chance test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed as label corruption increases.
Perfect fitting of shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Appending irrelevant features and permuting auxiliary proxy targets do not test this.

Corruption beyond 20% through fully random labels; approach to chance; perfect fit at each severity; and direct separation of signal learning from noise memorization. The extracted aggregates do not establish monotonic degradation at every severity.
Necessity or sufficiency of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation for random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Temporal order of learning real patterns versus memorizing noisy labels.

missing.what: Per-severity neural-model clean-test ACC/AUC results, including the clean baseline, needed to assess whether degradation is steady rather than merely present between endpoints. Figure 3 contains the curves, but exact intermediate values are not recoverable from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Selected labels are always changed to a different class, rather than replaced with an unrestricted uniform label. Neural models train for 100 epochs. Nonperfect aggregate training accuracy qualifies the tested protocol but does not establish inability to fit with longer training.

versions.untested_parts: Completely random labels, zero or near-zero training error, chance test error, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time cost relative to true labels and convergence speed as corruption grows.
Shuffled, independently permuted, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Tests only expected training-label corruption ratios up to 0.20 and clean-test performance. It does not test corruption rising to all labels, perfect training fit at each rate, or a steady rise toward chance.
Does not test weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal against random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
Does not measure the order in which real-label patterns and noisy or random labels are learned.

rows.operation_detail: Train with independently corrupted training labels; evaluate on the clean test set across label-noise ratios.

conditions.value: 16 datasets shared between OpenML-CC18 and TabZilla

rows.measure: Average accuracy and AUC under noisy-label corruption, reported as APS and WSP across evaluated severities.
rows.note: Reports aggregate test performance across corruption severity, not test error at 100% random labels or training fit at each severity.
rows.check: Values are correct. Add clean ACC/AUC baseline 0.876/0.936 from Table II. WSP is performance specifically at 20% corruption; APS integrates severity including the clean baseline. These measures establish degradation but not perfect training fit or monotonicity at every severity.
